newsitem.title: USA: Corn Belt seen due for colder, wetter weather.
newsitem.headline: Corn Belt seen due for colder, wetter weather.

text.p: Colder, wetter weather was seen heading for most of the U.S. Corn Belt beginning Wednesday night, private forecasters said.

"Tonight and tomorrow (Thursday) we're seeing rainfall of 0.5 to 1.5 inches across the (corn) belt, with a high percentage of coverage," said Joel Burgio, forecaster with Weather Services Corp. in Lexington, Mass.
As the front gradually moves out of the Midwest on Friday, the "tail-end of the system" could bring snow mixed with rain to some parts of Wisconsin and Minnesota, Burgio said.
Rainfall early Wednesday was largely confined to northern Illinois, forecasters said.
Low temperatures across the Corn Belt this weekend were seen falling to the upper 20s (degrees Fahrenheit) and low 30s, according to Weather Services Corp.

Another front will move across the belt during the early portion of next week, bringing more rain and cooler weather, according to the latest forecast from Jon Davis, meteorologist with Smith Barney brokerage.
Weather Express in Omaha, Neb. was forecasting a long-term pattern change Wednesday, with cold and wet weather dominating the Midwest the last ten days of October.
